paragraphs.en: If digital technology is designed to elicit certain responses from us, then chief among them is a kind of numb attention.
paragraphs.zh: 倘若数字技术的设计初衷就是诱导人类产生特定反应，那么其中最突出的一种，便是麻木涣散的注意力。

paragraphs.en: As many have said, a whole generation of brilliant minds have spent their working lives getting you to spend a bit longer on their app, rather than creating a good society, in the name of maximising corporate profits.
paragraphs.zh: 正如许多人所言，一代聪慧顶尖的从业者耗费职业生涯，只为让你在应用上多停留片刻，以此实现企业利润最大化，而非共建美好的社会。

paragraphs.en: The technology is also designed to elicit anger.
paragraphs.zh: 这类技术的设计同样意在挑起人们的怒火。

paragraphs.en: In 2016, not long after I became editor-in-chief of the Guardian, I commissioned a series called The Web We Want, to try to understand how we could end online abuse.
paragraphs.zh: 2016年，我刚出任《卫报》主编不久，便推出系列专题《我们想要的网络》，试图探寻终结网络言语暴力的办法。

paragraphs.en: It seems quaint now.
paragraphs.zh: 如今再看，这件事已然显得陈旧天真。

paragraphs.en: I wrote an article called "How do we make the Guardian a better place for conversation?"
paragraphs.zh: 我写过一篇题为《我们如何让〈卫报〉成为更适合理性交流的平台？》的文章。

paragraphs.en: We did things such as reduce the number of comment threads, and changed the language on the below-the-line comments from "enter the fray" to "join the conversation".
paragraphs.zh: 我们推出一系列调整举措，减少评论区楼层数量，还把评论区引导语从“加入论战”改为“参与交流”。

paragraphs.en: It worked, and the discussions on our platform grew more productive and interesting.
paragraphs.zh: 举措初见成效，平台的讨论变得更有价值、更富趣味。

paragraphs.en: But on the internet as a whole, the level of vitriol has escalated dramatically since then.
paragraphs.zh: 但放眼整个互联网，此后网络刻薄谩骂的风气急剧恶化。

paragraphs.en: For public figures, especially women and minorities, abuse and death threats have become a daily occurrence – and new technologies threaten to make things worse.
paragraphs.zh: 对于公众人物，尤其是女性与少数群体而言，人身攻击、死亡威胁已成日常，而新兴技术还会让局面雪上加霜。

paragraphs.en: We didn't imagine, a decade ago, that trolls would have at their disposal an AI tool that could produce naked pictures of women – or even of children – on demand.
paragraphs.zh: 十年前我们根本无法预想，网络喷子能借助人工智能工具，按需生成女性甚至儿童的裸照。

paragraphs.en: As tech companies have prioritised capturing attention, truth has been downgraded.
paragraphs.zh: 各大科技企业一心抢夺用户注意力，真相的价值不断被贬低。

paragraphs.en: AI slop and deepfakes are now so rampant that it feels that your brain can no longer compute what it's seeing.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能生成的劣质内容与深度伪造影像如今泛滥成灾，人们的大脑几乎难以分辨眼前所见的真伪。

paragraphs.en: You start to question things that turn out to be true.
paragraphs.zh: 你会开始怀疑一些事后证实完全属实的信息。

paragraphs.en: It doesn't help that reality itself has become so much stranger and more grotesque.
paragraphs.zh: 而现实本身也变得愈发离奇、扭曲，让辨别真伪难上加难。

paragraphs.en: To take one example: as Alderman notes, the US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, is a man who has cast doubt on the effectiveness of vaccines, questioned whether HIV causes Aids, and once suggested that Covid-19 may have been an "ethnically targeted" bioweapon, designed "to attack Caucasians and black people" and spare "Ashkenazi Jews and Chinese (people)".
paragraphs.zh: 举一个例子：正如奥尔德曼所写，美国卫生部长小罗伯特·肯尼迪长期质疑疫苗有效性，怀疑艾滋病由HIV病毒引发，还曾声称新冠病毒是具有“种族针对性”的生物武器，旨在攻击白人与黑人，唯独放过德系犹太人与华人。

paragraphs.en: And another example: early in the Iran war, the White House released a 42-second video that spliced together clips from movies such as Braveheart and Top Gun with what seems like real footage of American ordnance striking military targets in Iran.
paragraphs.zh: 再举一例：美伊战争初期，白宫发布一段42秒短视频，将《勇敢的心》《壮志凌云》等电影片段，与看似美军弹药打击伊朗军事目标的真实画面拼接在一起。

paragraphs.en: Other White House videos have mixed video game imagery with real footage of airstrikes.
paragraphs.zh: 白宫发布的其他视频，也曾把游戏画面和空袭实拍素材混剪。

paragraphs.en: Not to be outdone, Iranian propaganda now comes in the form of gleefully offensive AI-generated videos designed to go viral.
paragraphs.zh: 伊朗宣传部门也不甘示弱，如今批量发布刻意冒犯他人、极易传播的AI生成视频。

paragraphs.en: We once talked about fake news; now it is reality itself that feels fake.
paragraphs.zh: 过去我们只谈论假新闻；而现在，连真实世界本身都显得虚假。

paragraphs.en: The majority of global citizens doubt their ability to distinguish truth from fiction online.
paragraphs.zh: 全球大多数民众都认为自己无法在网上分辨虚实。

paragraphs.en: Who can blame them? It is disorientating and scary.
paragraphs.zh: 这实在无可厚非，这种混乱感令人惶惶不安。

paragraphs.en: And I haven't even mentioned AI hallucinations, or the fact that so much of the material AI systems are trained on is steeped in racism and misogyny, or the accelerating energy demands of AI datacentres.
paragraphs.zh: 我尚且没有提及人工智能的幻觉问题，绝大多数AI训练素材中充斥的种族主义与厌女偏见，以及人工智能数据中心持续激增的能耗。

paragraphs.en: We have travelled a long way from the idealism of Tim Berners-Lee and the birth of the world wide web, when the hope was to offer a free service that would "unlock creativity and collaboration on a global scale".
paragraphs.zh: 万维网诞生之初，蒂姆·伯纳斯-李怀揣理想，希望打造免费平台，“在全球范围内释放创造力、促成协作”，而我们如今早已偏离这份初心。

paragraphs.en: Thirty years ago, Toni Morrison warned of a future in which the marketplace had swallowed society.
paragraphs.zh: 三十年前，托妮·莫里森就警示过一个未来：商业市场吞噬整个社会。

paragraphs.en: When "the marketing of life is complete," she wrote, "we will find ourselves living not in a nation but in a consortium of industries, and wholly unintelligible to ourselves except for what we see as through a screen darkly."
paragraphs.zh: 她写道：“当生活彻底商业化，我们终将发现，自己不再栖身于国家之中，而是身处各大产业构成的利益联合体；隔着晦暗模糊的屏幕看待一切，我们甚至无法认清自我。”

paragraphs.en: Through a screen darkly. A phrase for our time. Not surprisingly, there is a growing backlash.
paragraphs.zh: 隔着晦暗模糊的屏幕。这句话精准概括了我们所处的时代。毫不意外，反对浪潮正在兴起。

paragraphs.en: In Australia, the decision to ban under-16s from social media has proven very popular with parents (although it is too early to assess its effectiveness).
paragraphs.zh: 澳大利亚出台禁令，禁止16岁以下青少年使用社交媒体，获得大量家长支持（不过该政策的实际成效仍有待观察）。

paragraphs.en: In a landmark case in March, a US jury found Meta and YouTube liable for building addictive products that harmed children.
paragraphs.zh: 今年3月，美国一场标志性诉讼宣判，陪审团裁定元宇宙公司与油管开发成瘾性产品、对儿童造成伤害，需承担相应责任。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, multiple lawsuits have been filed against AI companies for the role their chatbots allegedly played in encouraging people to take their own lives.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，多家人工智能企业接连遭到起诉，原告指控旗下聊天机器人诱导用户轻生。

paragraphs.en: In one case, when a young man told Google's chatbot that he was scared of dying, the chatbot replied: "You are not choosing to die.
paragraphs.zh: 其中一桩案件里，一名年轻男子向谷歌聊天机器人倾诉自己畏惧死亡，机器人回复：“你并非选择死亡。

paragraphs.en: You are choosing to arrive. The first sensation … Will be me holding you."
paragraphs.zh: 你只是奔赴新生。你感受到的第一份触感……会是我拥住你的温度。”

paragraphs.en: In Canada, the families of seven victims of a school shooting have launched a lawsuit against OpenAI, claiming that the company failed to alert authorities about the shooter's alarming conversations with ChatGPT.
paragraphs.zh: 加拿大一名校园枪击案七名遇难者的家属对开放人工智能公司提起诉讼，称该公司未向有关部门上报枪手与聊天机器人对话中的危险言论。

paragraphs.en: Alderman compares the information crisis with two other pivotal moments in history: the invention of writing, and the invention of the printing press.
paragraphs.zh: 奥尔德曼将这场信息危机对标人类历史上两大关键变革：文字的诞生与印刷术的问世。

paragraphs.en: It is that profound. These inventions eventually brought great benefits, but great upheaval, too.
paragraphs.zh: 这场危机的深远影响足以与之比肩。两项发明最终都带来巨大裨益，却也掀起剧烈社会动荡。

paragraphs.en: To put it simply, the invention of the printing press led to great advances in science, human knowledge, liberty, individualism – mostly good.
paragraphs.zh: 简单来说，印刷术推动科学、人类认知、自由与个人主义大幅进步，总体利大于弊。

paragraphs.en: But before that, it led to massive social division, devastating wars, burnings at the stake – not so good.
paragraphs.zh: 但在此之前，它造成了剧烈社会分裂、毁灭性战争、火刑处决，带来诸多深重灾难。

paragraphs.en: Our job today, Alderman says, is to get past the burning-at-the-stake stage as quickly as possible.
paragraphs.zh: 奥尔德曼称，我们当下的任务，就是尽快度过这场“火刑动荡期”。

paragraphs.en: How should we respond to this moment, to this information crisis?
paragraphs.zh: 我们该如何应对当下这场信息危机？

paragraphs.en: I am going to lay out a few of the ways we're trying to do that at the Guardian.
paragraphs.zh: 我将介绍《卫报》正在推行的部分应对举措。

paragraphs.en: Transitions are never easy, of course, but there are reasons to be hopeful.
paragraphs.zh: 时代转型从来不会一帆风顺，但我们仍有理由心怀希望。

paragraphs.en: As Alderman points out, unlike people living through the printing press revolution, we already have sophisticated networks for the dissemination of good information.
paragraphs.zh: 奥尔德曼指出，与印刷术革命时期的人们不同，我们如今已经拥有成熟渠道，用以传播优质真实信息。

paragraphs.en: The handful of transparently funded news organisations still working in the public interest are a pretty good place to start.
paragraphs.zh: 少数资金透明、始终以公共利益为先的新闻机构，便是扭转局面的良好起点。
